title: RBAC session boundary enforcer + automated evidence collector for periodic reviews
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: Auditors and enterprise customers require (1) deterministic attestations about who had access to tenant-scoped resources, (2) reproducible evidence bundles (signed) for periodic access reviews, and (3) enforcement at session boundary to ensure short-lived elevated privileges don’t persist across SSO sessions. Current exports capture grants but lack session-scoped deltas and end-to-end proof tying SCIM/SSO events to KMS-signed evidence bundles by residency.

Goal: Implement a session-bound enforcement layer that can: (a) evaluate RBAC at token/session-issue time and at gateway boundary, (b) emit compact signed event fragments for every change (grant/revoke/session-start/session-end), and (c) produce automated evidence packs consumable by auditors and the periodic access-review UI. Evidence packs should include residency metadata, retention tags, and KMS signatures to prove non-repudiation.

Scope: Deliver server-side enforcement (gateway + token service) and an evidence pipeline: SCIM delta stream consumer, SSO/SAML assertion correlator, RBAC-policy-change hook, and an evidence assembler that outputs tenant-scoped ZIPs with manifest.json, signed-event-log.ndjson, and retention-policy.txt. Out of scope: full UI for review (PM will own), long-term cold storage (use existing retention export bucket).

Design decisions & trade-offs: 
- Enforce on gateway vs token: we will keep token-issuance checks (short TTL) and add gateway boundary checks for delegated sessions to avoid replay/latency issues in high-throughput paths.
- Evidence signature model: use envelope signing via customer-specific KMS keys when present, otherwise platform key with tenant-acknowledgement header. This balances enterprise needs and platform operability.
- Event format: ndjson with one canonical event type per line; this simplifies streaming and incremental assembly for reviewers.

Acceptance Criteria:
1) Gateway rejects any request where RBAC policy resolves to deny for the active session after a SCIM revoke event has been processed (end-to-end within configured SLA).
2) Evidence assembler produces a signed ZIP for a tenant for any requested date range containing manifest.json, signed-event-log.ndjson, and retention-policy.txt.
3) Periodic access-review cron triggers the assembler and uploads to s3://redwood-compliance-exports/{tenant}/{YYYY-MM-DD}/evidence.zip with metadata residency=eu-west-1 for EU tenants.
4) Integration tests covering SCIM revoke -> gateway enforcement and full evidence bundle verification (signature verified with KMS).

Implementation notes: 
- New service: access-evidence-assembler (Go); subscribes to internal pubsub topic "access-events-v2".
- Gateway hooks: fast path consult to in-memory cache of last policy decision; on cache miss or policy-change event consult policy-service.
- SCIM: continue using current reconcile stream; add translator that emits canonical access events (user.created, user.deactivated, membership.added, membership.removed).
- Storage: evidence zip staged in per-region bucket then lifecycle moved based on retention tags.

Rollout plan: Canary in staging -> opt-in beta with 3 tenants (internal, partner A, large enterprise) -> 1-week observation -> wide rollout. Fallback: assembler can re-run for historical ranges; gateway can be toggled to legacy mode via feature flag.

Risks: KMS key management complexity when tenants manage keys; potential latency impact on gateway decisions under bursty traffic (we mitigate with TTL and async revocation scanning).

Documentation & artifacts: PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/COMPL/Session+Boundary+Evidence+PRD, Design diagrams: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2ExampleDesign, Runbook stub: https://wiki.redwood.ai/runbooks/access-evidence, Initial GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/18902, Integration test dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ABCD-evidence-integ
acceptance_criteria: Gateway rejects sessions after SCIM revoke processed within SLA
Assembler returns signed evidence ZIP with manifest and signed-event-log
Croned access-review produces per-tenant evidence in regional bucket with residency metadata
Integration tests validate signature and enforcement behavior

2026-02-23 - Spike complete: measured gateway added ~1.8ms median latency for in-cache checks. PRD updated with latency budget and fallback flag.

2026-03-05 - Security review requested. Recorded concerns about cross-region evidence transfer; security suggested additional envelope metadata and hash-chaining events.
2026-03-10 - QA repro steps added to runbook. Observed SCIM delta ordering edge-case; temporary mitigation: apply watermark ordering and idempotent event application.
2026-03-12 - Blocker removed: KMS team approved key ACL model. Next steps: add integration tests and schedule canary with partner tenant on 2026-03-17.
